shared_elements: large monolithic anthropomorphic block/pillar carved in low relief
row of repeated arch/loop-shaped motifs across the upper zone
horizontal band or belt-like divider running across the body
curved paired loops or nested crescent shapes
suspended element hanging below the belt band on the lower body
justification: Both surfaces treat a large upright anthropomorphic monolith as a body: an upper register of repeated arch/loop shapes, a horizontal belt-like band across the torso, discs and curved paired motifs above it, and a pendant element hanging below the band — a fairly specific shared scheme of ornamenting a figure's front. The decisive difference is subject matter within that scheme: B is populated with recognisable creatures (quadrupeds in profile, a long-necked bird, a serpentine form) and net/zigzag patterning, whereas A confines itself to abstract rings, loops and bands with a modelled face, showing no animals at all.
